profile.headline: Software Engineer at NIH - NIAID
profile.summary: I’m a software engineer with a passion for (and proven track record in) developing beautiful, engaging and high-performance web applications using the latest cloud and web technologies.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Develop a web-based data processing, exploration & visualization platform for electron microscopy.
- Member of the Bioinformatics and Computational Biosciences Branch of NIAID. Employed via Guidehouse, a federal contractor.

positions.description: Work closely with a team of scientists to develop web applications for exploring complex genetic data sets.

positions.title: Front-End Developer
positions.description:
- Lead the front-end development of the Atlas of Economic Complexity (http://atlas.cid.harvard.edu), an online data visualization platform that allows people to explore global trade flows across the world and discover new growth opportunities.
- Train and supervise junior developers.

positions.title: Front-End Developer
positions.description:
- I work closely with senior developers, designers and project managers to create web applications that bring complex data sets to life, using a mix of HTML, CSS and JavaScript/TypeScript. 
- Clients worked for: Twitter, NBC News, Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, US Patents & Trademark Office, Tennessee Department of Education, Pacific Salmon Foundation.

honors.title: Finalist (Politics & Global category), Kantar Information is Beautiful Awards 2018 and 2019
honors.description: This honor goes to the Atlas of Economic Complexity, for which I was the lead front-end developer. The Kantar Information is Beautiful Awards recognize the best works in the field of data visualization and information design every year from around the world. There were 10 finalists out of 112 entries in the category in 2018 and 8 out of 88 entries in 2019.
honors.issuer: Issued by Kantar Information is Beautiful Awards · Nov 2019

honors.title: Finalist - LeRoy Apker Award
honors.description: I was one of six undergrads in the country shortlisted as a finalist by the American Physical Society (from a large pool of students nominated by their colleges) for the Leroy Apker Award. The award recognizes the best undergraduate physics research in the US annually, and is also the highest honor for a physics major in the country.
honors.issuer: Issued by American Physical Society · Jul 2014

projects.title: Quantum Monte Carlo calculation of the imaginary-time Green’s function in the Hubbard model
projects.description:
- My undergraduate thesis is in the area of quantum Monte Carlo, a computational method in condensed matter physics. 
- In my thesis, I formulated a quantum Monte Carlo algorithm to compute imaginary-time correlation functions in the ground state of the Hubbard model, which is widely believed to describe high-temperature superconductors.
- This work was selected by the American Physical Society (APS) as one of six finalists for the LeRoy Apker Award, recognizing the best undergraduate physics research in the US annually. 
- To learn more, visit www.huy.dev/Reed-thesis

projects.title: Measurement Learning & Improvement Study (Gates Foundation)
projects.description:
- Interactive teacher survey and visualization of survey results for the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. 
- JavaScript libraries used:
  + React (view layer)
  + Backbone, Backbone.Radio (model layer, eventing system)
  + jQuery (AJAX, DOM manipulation)
  + LoDash (utilities)
- Other tools used:
  + TypeScript (scripting language)
  + Grunt (build tool)
  + Compass/SASS (CSS preprocessor)
